source.title: Finedeep: Mitigating Sparse Activation in Dense LLMs via Multi-Layer Fine-Grained Experts
source.authors: Leiyu Pan; Zhenpeng Su; Min-Xuan Lv; Yizhe Xiong; Xiangwen Zhang; Zijia Lin; Hui Chen; Jun-Gong Han; Gui-Guang Ding; Cheng Luo; Di Zhang; Kun Gai; De-Yi Xiong

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports held-out perplexity for architecture variants with comparable parameter counts, bearing on whether architecture details change loss only slightly. It does not measure or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws as background but does not sweep parameters, tokens, or compute to fit scaling curves, test extrapolation, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Rows below cover reported Pile test-set PPL for the architecture configurations. Downstream benchmark scores and activation analyses do not measure the loss behavior named in V4.
record.test_reason: This paper proposes an architecture (Finedeep). It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background in the introduction. It fits no power laws, tests no extrapolation and studies no compute-optimal allocation. Its Pile PPL tables compare the authors' own method against a dense baseline and against its own variants. They do not sweep conventional transformer depth, width or other shape hyperparameters at fixed size, so they are not a test of V4. That makes them comparisons of the study's own method, not results on the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Finedeep significantly outperforms dense models of near-identical parameter count and FLOPs in Pile PPL and benchmark scores. They find it works best when sub-layer count and experts per sub-layer are balanced, and that it mitigates sparse activation.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and pre-trains a modified dense architecture with partitioned FFNs and multi-layer expert arrangements; it does not reproduce a scaling-law measurement or fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Pile PPL varies with the number of expert sub-layers and experts per sub-layer, and with the routing normalization choice (sigmoid versus softmax).

fits_no_version.finding: At near-identical parameter counts and FLOPs, rearranging the FFN into M sub-layers of K experts changes Pile PPL by at most about 2% (e.g. Medium 12.42 dense vs 12.13 at M=4/K=4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, restructuring the FFN into multi-sub-layer fine-grained experts changes loss only slightly. This is loosely related to V4, but it is a novel-architecture comparison, not a shape sweep.

record.problems: The architecture comparisons cover only the reported model sizes and configurations; the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for PPL. Its limitation section says training was limited to 100B tokens and the largest model to 7.5B parameters.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant Pile PPL result was left out. Downstream benchmark results and activation-distribution/NSAR analyses were not recorded as rows because they do not measure V4's loss outcome.

untested.parts: All: no extrapolation from fitted small runs.
No sweep of depth, width, heads or other shape hyperparameters in a standard transformer at fixed parameter count.
All: no other modalities or training regimes.
All: downstream scores are not related to scale or loss in any predictive fit.
All: no fitting choices are examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's guess (tests, T2, V4 supports) is rejected. The PPL tables are the study's own method compared with its baseline and its own ablations. They are not a test of V4's claim about conventional depth and width. All runs use a single training budget of 100B tokens, three sizes, and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small runs predict substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as compute changes.
The study varies Finedeep expert-sub-layer and expert counts, but does not broadly sweep conventional transformer depth, width, or other architectures.
Other modalities and training regimes, including repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices and setup.
